Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the in-line citation matches the actual text from the article. The citation in the bibliography is from Greetham's article, specifically pages 45-46. The in-line citation says: “obscured not by a 'cloak of print' but by the veil of scribal confusion and mis-transmission” (Greetham 45-46). 

I remember that when I looked up the article using the DOI, I found that the text on pages 45-46 actually uses the phrase "veil of print" instead of "cloak of print". So the mistake here is that the in-line citation used "cloak" instead of "veil". 

I think the error occurred in the step where the in-line citation was created. The person who made the citation must have misread or incorrectly recalled the phrase from the article. So the agent responsible is the one who wrote the in-line citation, probably the author or a researcher who cited the work. 

Looking at the conversation, the first mistake was when the in-line citation was created, so that would be step 1. The reason is that they incorrectly used "cloak" instead of "veil" from the original text.
